details:
Abandoned but not Forgotten – Team 369

Our project is an interactive educational website that highlights human-made space hardware left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space. It explores abandoned, inactive, destroyed, and still-operational spacecraft, landers, orbiters, and other mission equipment.

The website is divided into three main sections: Moon, Mars, and Deep Space. Users can explore different NASA missions, discover what remains from each mission, access additional information through reference links, and test their knowledge through an interactive quiz game.

Purpose and Benefits: The main goal is to spread awareness about the history and legacy of space exploration, promote curiosity about NASA missions, and encourage interactive learning. It helps people understand that off-world hardware is not simply space junk but also represents important achievements in human engineering and scientific discovery.

Technology and Tools: We developed a website-based learning experience with interactive sections, educational content, reference links, and a quiz game. We used NASA's scientific resources and mission information to support our research.

Impact: Our project makes space exploration history easier and more interesting to understand, especially for students and young learners. It encourages people to explore the remains of past missions and appreciate how previous discoveries contribute to future space exploration.

Our creative approach combines space history, interactive learning, and technology to make learning about forgotten space hardware engaging and informative.
